text:
marta: Quick internal announcement 1: we deployed hybrid-prefetch-v4 + adaptive-burst to hosted canary (15%) at 1767770001. Posting early telemetry and rollout plan here. :rocket:

deploy-bot: release marta/hybrid-prefetch-v4 -> canary (15%) succeeded. details: https://internal.redwood/deploys/1767770001

marta: Early canary vs baseline (same traffic slice): p50 ~15% lower (66ms -> 56ms), p99 ~22% lower (410ms -> 320ms), token cost per request ~10% lower. GPU busy fraction down ~6%.

sam: Nice. Any differences across model families?

marta: Short summary: small/lightweight models: modest p50 wins (~8%) and cost down. mid-size LLMs (common routes) saw the largest benefits. very long-context routes (>1500 tokens) saw neutral p50 and small p99 (+2-4%) in a handful of routes due to microbatch alignment; cost still improves. Full per-model/per-length breakdown is in the dashboard: https://internal.redwood/telemetry/hybrid-prefetch-v4-canary

rachel: Product question: could this change visible latency for end-users or cause any output variance?

marta: No model-behavior changes expected 1 5. This is purely serving-layer prefetch and burst-control. We ran the eval regression suite and found no semantic diffs. If anyone spots anomalies, tag #eng-runtime immediately.

tom: Ops: whats the rollback key and operator command?

marta: Rollback/runbook live: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/hybrid-prefetch-v4-runbook. Rollback flag and command below:

```
# rollback
redwoodctl feature set hybrid_prefetch.v4=false --scope=hosted --selector=canary
```

infra: Heads-up 1: updated the GPU utilization alerts and memory thresholds for the canary pool. We'll monitor for unusual OOMs or evictions.

sam: Suggest adding a 5m long-context smoke in the canary pipeline that runs a couple ~2k token prompts to catch edge cases.

marta: Agreed 1 51. I'll add the smoke test step tonight and post when it's live.

product: Please cc infra@ and product-sre@ when you move to 50% so oncall can be ready to watch the dashboards.

marta: Will do. Rollout plan in runbook: remain at 15% for 24h, if p99 stable we move to 50% then 100% over the next 48h. We'll publish a short retro with econ tables and per-route notes after 72h.

sam: Thanks 69 great work. Shoutout to the runtime team (Marta, Jin, Arif, Lena) for iterating on the prefetch heuristics and the burst controller. :tada:

marta: Thanks team 1. If you own latency-sensitive routes, please check your dashboards and comment on the runbook if you want to opt out of the dedicated rollout.
